title: Unnecessary Box Pinning of Unpin Futures (Allocation Bloat)
pattern: An asynchronous function systematically wraps its return future in `Box::pin` and returns a trait object (`Pin<Box<dyn Future>>`) to avoid putting complex nested generic types in its signature.
why_bad: Locally, the function signature is highly "clean" and simple. Globally, it introduces substantial runtime allocation overhead. Wrapping every single intermediate future in a heap allocation (`Box`) adds massive memory footprint and cache pollution, completely negating the zero-cost promise of Rust's async state machines.
detection: Asynchronous helper functions that do not require dynamic dispatch returning `Pin<Box<dyn Future>>` instead of using the static `impl Future` type erasure.
counterexample: Valid when implementing complex recursive async functions where static type sizing is impossible, or when dynamic dispatch is explicitly required by a trait boundary. Mark `Context-dependent`.
source: Jon Gjengset, *Rust for Rustaceans*, Chapter 9, "Asynchronous Rust: Dynamic Dispatch" (p. 153).
